Name: Gunslinger
Level Up: Beat a game while having defeated enemies only with ranged attacks
Description: +2 Agility. Pistol, Steady Hand, Akimbo.
What it is there: A Mutant calling: +2 Agility, Pistol, Steady Hand, Akimbo.
Why it fits: A Mutant calling built on pistols and Agility. Dash is the closest verb to Agility, and a ranged-only win is a level-up any game with ranged attacks can host.

Name: Marauder
Level Up: Beat a game while only ever attacking up close
Description: +2 Strength. Axe, Dismember, Charge, Butchery.
What it is there: A Mutant calling: +2 Strength, Axe, Dismember, Charge.
Why it fits: The axe calling: Strength, charging in and dismembering. Bash and the higher Health say brawler, and its level-up is the Gunslinger's opposite, so the two read as a pair from one game.

Name: Water Merchant
Level Up: Beat a game while having bought something from a shop
Description: +2 Ego. Short Blade, Snake Oiler. Starts with trade goods.
What it is there: A Mutant calling: +2 Ego, starts with trade goods and +200 with the water barons.
Why it fits: In Qud fresh water is the currency, and the Water Merchant starts rich in trade goods with +200 reputation with the water barons. Here that is extra Gold for less Health: a shop-led run.

Name: Tinker
Level Up: Beat a game while having crafted or upgraded an item
Description: +2 Intelligence. Tinkering: Disassemble, Repair, Lay Mine, Tinker I. Begins with random artifacts and scrap.
What it is there: A Mutant calling: +2 Intelligence, the tinkering tree, starts with artifacts and scrap.
Why it fits: The calling that takes things apart and builds new ones. Transmute is this game's turning-one-thing-into-another verb, and 'random artifacts and scrap' becomes a random trinket.

Name: Valkyrie
Level Up: Beat a game while having defeated a boss in close combat
Description: A cold-resistant, stealthy warrior with a long sword and a dagger. The easiest role in the game.
What it is there: Human or dwarf, always female; starts with a +1 long sword, +0 dagger, small shield, cold resistance and stealth.
Why it fits: The role new players are told to start with: the highest Health of any character here, and a plain fighter's level-up.

Name: Wizard
Level Up: Beat a game while having defeated an enemy with a spell
Description: Frail, but starts with force bolt, a cloak of magic resistance, a random wand and three random scrolls.
What it is there: Starts with a quarterstaff, cloak of magic resistance, a random wand, two random rings, potions, three random scrolls and the force bolt spellbook.
Why it fits: Low Health and a bag of unknown magic: Transmute and Random for a hero who changes things rather than hits them.

Name: Tourist
Level Up: Beat a game while having spent all your gold in it
Description: Starts with a lot of gold, a Hawaiian shirt and an expensive camera. Everyone overcharges them.
What it is there: Starts with up to 1000 gold, darts, a Hawaiian shirt, an expensive camera, food and four scrolls of magic mapping; shopkeepers charge tourists more.
Why it fits: The joke role, and a real playstyle here: lowest Health, triple the Gold, a shop-led run. Its loadout is the Magic Mapping candidate, as in NetHack.

Name: Archeologist
Level Up: Beat a game while having found a secret area
Description: Fast, with a pick-axe, a bullwhip and a tinning kit; digs through anything.
What it is there: Starts fast with a pick-axe, a +2 bullwhip, a tinning kit and a touchstone; can dig through walls and floors from turn one.
Why it fits: Intrinsic speed and digging read as Dash; finding secrets is what an archeologist does in any game. The pick-axe becomes the Wand of Digging candidate.

Name: Healer
Level Up: Beat a game while having healed someone other than yourself
Description: Starts rich, with a stethoscope, healing spells and a wand of sleep, but is weak in a fight.
What it is there: Starts with 1001-2000 gold, a scalpel, a stethoscope, healing spellbooks, potions and a wand of sleep; poison resistant.
Why it fits: A support hero with money and no punch. Its loadout is the Wand of Sleep candidate, as in NetHack.

Name: Felid
Level Up: Beat a game without equipping anything
Description: A cat: no armour, no weapons, very hard to hit, and nine lives.
What it is there: A small quadruped species that can't wear armour or wield weapons but evades well, and gains extra lives as it levels.
Why it fits: Crawl's most beloved species. The extra lives are the hook: a hero who dies and keeps going. Loot it can't carry suits a no-equipment level-up.

Name: Minotaur
Level Up: Beat a game while having countered an attack
Description: Horns, a headbutt counter-attack, and the strength of the classic Minotaur Berserker.
What it is there: A strong melee species with horns; it counter-attacks with a headbutt when it dodges. 'MiBe' (Minotaur Berserker) is the standard beginner pick.
Why it fits: The genre's favourite brute, and the counter-attack is a level-up any action game can host.

Name: Demigod
Level Up: Beat a game without any help from a god
Description: Half divine, so no god will take them; gains attributes faster than anyone instead.
What it is there: A species that can't worship any god but gains four attribute points every three levels instead of two every six.
Why it fits: Zagreus levels up WITH a god's help; the Demigod is the opposite. Random suits divine attributes arriving unasked.

Name: Warrior
Level Up: Beat a game while having repaired a weapon or armour
Description: The fighter: the most Strength and Vitality, and can repair his own gear.
What it is there: Diablo I's fighter class; his skill is Item Repair, which restores durability at a cost to maximum durability.
Why it fits: The plain brawler of the original trio; repairing gear is a thing most games with durability or upgrades let you do.

Name: Rogue
Level Up: Beat a game while having disarmed a trap
Description: The archer: the most Dexterity, the only class good with a bow, and disarms traps.
What it is there: Diablo I's ranged class; her skill is Trap Disarm, and she uses bows better than anyone.
Why it fits: Trap disarming is the Rogue's own skill and a common roguelike action.

Name: Sorcerer
Level Up: Beat a game while having recharged an item
Description: The caster: the most Magic and mana, and can recharge staves.
What it is there: Diablo I's spellcaster; his skill is Staff Recharge.
Why it fits: Recharging is the Sorcerer's skill, and charges are already a system here (Charged items, wands).

Name: Willow
Level Up: Beat a game while having started a fire
Description: A firestarter who carries a lighter and doesn't burn.
What it is there: Obsessed with fire; starts with a Lighter and takes no damage from fire.
Why it fits: Fire is already a tile and a status here; Willow is the hero built on it.

Name: Wolfgang
Level Up: Beat a game while having eaten 3 or more things
Description: A strongman who is mighty when well fed and wimpy when hungry.
What it is there: Gets stronger and bigger the fuller his hunger meter, and weaker when hungry.
Why it fits: The brute, with a level-up about food (the food family is the largest loot tag).

Name: Wendy
Level Up: Beat a game with a companion fighting beside you
Description: Starts with Abigail's flower; her twin sister's ghost fights beside her.
What it is there: Summons Abigail, her twin's ghost, who fights for her.
Why it fits: The companion hero; allies are among the most common goals in the research.
Needs: new: an ally on the board

Name: WX-78
Level Up: Beat a game while having upgraded yourself
Description: A robot who upgrades itself by eating gears, and hates all living things.
What it is there: An automaton that crafts circuits for quirks (originally, gained stats by eating gears).
Why it fits: Self-upgrade reads as Transmute; a robot hero for the robot tag's sake.

Name: Jester
Level Up: Beat a game while having rerolled a reward or a level-up
Description: The wild card: no stat bonuses, and abilities pulled at random from every other class.
What it is there: An unlockable class whose ability pool draws from all the others; its only stat modifier is a Level Up Reroll.
Why it fits: Random and Scramble are the reroll verbs; the level-up is the Jester's one fixed trait.

Name: Thief
Level Up: Beat a game while having stolen something
Description: Fast and lucky: great movement, stealth, and a solid ranged attack.
What it is there: Gains Speed and Luck (at the cost of Strength and Constitution); abilities for movement and staying stealthy.
Why it fits: Speed reads as Dash, and stealing is something many games allow; the Theft ability is the enemies' version.

Name: Necromancer
Level Up: Beat a game while having stolen health from an enemy
Description: Tough, and steals health from everything it hits with leeches.
What it is there: Gains Constitution and Charisma; every Necromancer can steal health from other units with leeches, which stack without limit.
Why it fits: Life steal is a hero trait nobody has here (King Leoric has it as an enemy).

Name: Keeper
Level Up: Beat a game while carrying as much gold as you can hold
Description: Coins are his health: he heals by picking up money.
What it is there: A secret character (Afterbirth) whose health is coin hearts, refilled by picking up pennies; starts with a bomb and a triple shot.
Why it fits: Gold as health is a new economy for one hero. Wooden Nickel (a live relic) is the starting item Keeper earns in Isaac.

Name: The Lost
Level Up: Beat a game after dying once in it
Description: No health at all: dies to any hit, but flies and sees through walls.
What it is there: A secret character with no health who dies from any damage; starts with flight, spectral tears and (once unlocked) the D4 and Holy Mantle.
Why it fits: The genre's glass cannon, and dying-then-winning is its own level-up. D6 is live. Health 1 is below the spec's 5-10 on purpose: dying to any hit is the character.

Name: Plague Doctor
Level Up: Beat a game while having poisoned an enemy
Description: "What better laboratory than the blood-soaked battlefield?" Throws plague grenades and treats disease.
What it is there: A support hero whose signature is the Plague Grenade (blight on the back ranks) and who cures blight and bleed.
Why it fits: Grenades read as Bombs; poisoning is a level-up most games with damage types allow.

Name: Crusader
Level Up: Beat a game while having defeated an undead enemy
Description: "A mighty sword arm anchored by holy purpose." Strong against the unholy, and raises the light.
What it is there: A strong generalist who hits any rank, heals health and stress, and raises the Light Meter; deadly against the Unholy. Each Crusader brings a Holy Water.
Why it fits: The holy warrior; undead is the second most common enemy tag here (9 bodies).

Name: Antiquarian
Level Up: Beat a game while having found a treasure
Description: "She searches where others will not go." The weakest fighter, but finds more gold.
What it is there: The weakest damage dealer of all heroes, but a strong support; she finds extra gold and antiques on expeditions.
Why it fits: A treasure-hunter with extra Gold and the lowest Health, built for a shop-led run.

Name: Grave Robber
Level Up: Beat a game while having looted a grave, a body or a corpse
Description: "Gold gleams like a dagger's point." Fast, evasive, and good at looting curios.
What it is there: A rogue who throws daggers, dodges with Shadow Fade and handles curios with fewer risks.
Why it fits: Looting the dead is something most dungeon games allow; Dash for her speed.

Name: Mounties
Level Up: Beat a game while having defended a position until help arrived
Description: "Welcome to Canada, eh!" They guard the border with hockey sticks.
What it is there: Rare characters at the Canadian border (6 Strength and Fitness, 4 Vitality) who fight off the last zombies before the party crosses.
Why it fits: The end of the road as a hero; Bash for strength, Push for the stick's knockback.

Name: The Lamb
Level Up: Beat a game while having recruited a defeated enemy
Description: Saved by a god in chains, and wearing the Red Crown. Each run hands them a random weapon and curse.
What it is there: The protagonist: a lamb who survived sacrifice and leads a cult for The One Who Waits, with a weapon and a curse dealt at random each crusade.
Why it fits: A random weapon each run reads as Random; recruiting enemies into the flock is the game's heart.

Name: Busker
Level Up: Beat a game while having distracted an enemy
Description: "Rarely short of coin." Weak in a fair fight, but distracting, quick to flee, and paid to play.
What it is there: A class with Distraction (disrupts attacks on allies), Entertain (earns gold near towns and carnivals) and Elite Flee.
Why it fits: A coin-earning support hero: extra Gold, and Dash for fleeing.

Name: Treasure Hunter
Level Up: Beat a game while having opened a chest that turned out to be a trap or a mimic
Description: Finds hidden treasure where others don't, and isn't afraid of mimics.
What it is there: A class with Find Treasure (overworld treasure once a day) and Mimic Whisper (turns mimics into ordinary chests).
Why it fits: Mimics are in nearly every dungeon game; Keys suit a chest-opener.

Name: Will
Level Up: Beat a game while having sold something
Description: A merchant who always wanted to be a hero: runs the shop by day, delves the dungeons by night.
What it is there: The protagonist, heir to the Moonlighter shop, who sells what he finds in the dungeons to fund becoming a hero.
Why it fits: The shopkeeper hero: Gold to start, a roll (Dash), and a level-up about selling, which the Merchant Mirror would allow.

Name: Peasant
Level Up: Beat a game while having mined gold or ore out of a wall
Description: Sent down the mine with a pickaxe and a canary. When one dies, the next picks up half the gold.
What it is there: The only playable character: a randomly named peasant with a pickaxe, bombs and a Canary familiar. Each death makes a new peasant, who inherits half the previous one's gold.
Why it fits: A digger with a bomb and a bird: the mining is the level-up, the Canary the starting piece.

Name: The Beheaded
Level Up: Beat a game while having parried an attack
Description: A blob of cells that takes over a headless body. Dies, comes back, tries again.
What it is there: The protagonist: a shadowy, gas-like mass with a glowing crystal inside that possesses headless bodies, and rises again in the Prisoners' Quarters after every death.
Why it fits: The roll (Dash) and the swing (Bash); the level-up is the parry, Dead Cells' most rewarded move (shields parry, and parrying stuns most bosses).
Needs: new: a Rusty Sword weapon (the plain starter)

Name: Gambler
Level Up: Beat a game while having bet on a gamble and won
Description: Five damage, two, one, and three blanks. "100% skill." Or: "snake eyes..."
What it is there: A tier 2 orange hero whose die is half blanks and half damage (5, 2, 1), with his own lines for the best and worst roll.
Why it fits: A hero who is all variance: Random as his verb, a die as his piece, and a level-up about winning a bet.

Name: Captain
Level Up: Beat a game while having called in an air strike or a supply drop
Description: Commander of the UES Safe Travels. Calls things down from orbit.
What it is there: Commander of the UES Safe Travels, unlocked by beating Mithrix: a shotgun, a stun tazer, an orbital probe and supply beacons (healing, shock, resupply, hacking) dropped from his ship.
Why it fits: His orbital probe is the bomb, his tazer the stun; the level-up is calling something down from above.
Needs: new: a Supply Beacon piece (once a run: heal, or a free chest)
